rows.label: Share of Dogs Trust's 2025 international spending that went on rabies control (dog vaccination, rabies education and surveillance)

source.title: Dogs Trust Annual Report 2025 (year to 31 December 2025): consolidated SOFA, notes 1 and 7(a)

rows.explainer: Our judgment, read by both of charityevals' Dogs Trust models so the split is one number: the rabies model's cost is this share of the £26.1m international line, the dog-welfare model's the rest. The accounts don't split international work by activity. Anchor, one sum: 2.2 million doses at Goa's full cost of $3.45 in 2018-19 (Gibson et al. 2022), about $4.3 in 2025 prices, is about $9.5m, of which partners pay part (vaccine donated by MSD in Goa, government vaccinators in India's drives): we put Dogs Trust's spending per dose at about two thirds, $6.3m or £4.8m, plus rabies education and surveillance, about £0.5m. The grants to BSPCA, PDAFF Cambodia, Guinea, Bangladesh and Timor-Leste pay for doses inside the 2.2 million, so they are in that sum, not added; Soi Dog's and Hope & Animal Trust's catch-neuter-vaccinate work is in the dog-welfare model. £5.3m of £26.1m is 20%; 12% to 32% because WVS's split isn't published (its 2025 accounts, Charity Commission 1100485, will give the Mission Rabies fund).
